title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 22 (Execution of bills of exchange, etc.)

content.overview: Section 22(1) provides that a bill of exchange, hundi or promissory note shall be deemed to have been made, accepted, drawn or endorsed on behalf of a company if made, accepted, drawn or endorsed in the name of, or on behalf of or on account of, the company by any person acting under its authority, express or implied. Sub-section (2) allows a company, by writing under its common seal (if any), to authorise any person as its attorney to execute other deeds on its behalf in any place in or outside India; if the company has no common seal, the authorisation shall be made by two directors or by a director and the Company Secretary (where appointed). Sub-section (3) provides that a deed signed by such an attorney on behalf of the company and under his seal shall bind the company.
content.glance: Bills/hundis/notes bind if made under company authority; written attorney authorisation (common seal if any; else two directors or director+CS); attorney’s sealed deed binds the company.
content.study: A bill of exchange, hundi or promissory note is deemed to have been made, accepted, drawn or endorsed on behalf of the company if done in the name of, or on behalf or on account of, the company by any person acting under its authority, express or implied. A company may by writing under its common seal (if any) authorise any person, generally or for specified matters, as its attorney to execute other deeds on its behalf in or outside India. Where the company does not have a common seal, the authorisation must be made by two directors or by a director and the Company Secretary, wherever appointed. A deed signed by such an attorney on behalf of the company and under his seal binds the company. Current-law framing: identify the instrument or deed; test authority (express or implied for bills; written authorisation for deeds); apply the common-seal / no-seal rules; conclude binding effect.

sections.heading: Deemed company instrument (bills, hundis, notes)
sections.body: A bill of exchange, hundi or promissory note is deemed made, accepted, drawn or endorsed on behalf of the company if done in the name of, or on behalf or on account of, the company by any person acting under its authority, express or implied.

sections.heading: Attorney authorisation for deeds
sections.body: A company may by writing under its common seal (if any) authorise any person, generally or for specified matters, as its attorney to execute other deeds on its behalf in any place in or outside India. If the company has no common seal, the authorisation shall be made by two directors or by a director and the Company Secretary (where appointed).

sections.heading: Binding effect of attorney’s deed
sections.body: A deed signed by such an attorney on behalf of the company and under his seal shall bind the company.

provisions.title: Execution of bills of exchange, etc.

examples.title: Promissory note under implied authority
examples.body: An authorised officer draws a promissory note in the company’s name. Under section 22(1) it is deemed a company instrument.

examples.title: Attorney deed without common seal
examples.body: A company without a common seal authorises an attorney by writing signed by two directors. A deed signed by that attorney under his seal binds the company under section 22(2)–(3).

hypotheticals.question: Must every company instrument carry the common seal?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. For bills, hundis and promissory notes, section 22(1) looks to authority (express or implied). For other deeds, written authorisation under common seal (if any) or, if no seal, by two directors or director and CS, is required.

distinctions.title: Execution of bills/deeds (s. 22) vs authentication of documents (s. 21)
distinctions.left: How bills, notes and attorney deeds bind the company
distinctions.right: How documents, proceedings and contracts are authenticated

rows.right: Authentication of company documents and contracts

misconceptions.trap: Only formal Board resolution can create authority for a company bill.
misconceptions.correction: Section 22(1) covers any person acting under the company’s authority, express or implied.

misconceptions.trap: A company without a common seal cannot appoint an attorney for deeds.
misconceptions.correction: The proviso to section 22(2) allows authorisation by two directors or by a director and the Company Secretary.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 22 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the instrument or deed. II. Test authority under (1) or written authorisation under (2). III. Apply common-seal / no-seal rules. IV. Conclude binding effect under (1) or (3).

examTips: Separate bills/notes (authority) from attorney deeds (written authorisation).
State the no-common-seal proviso (two directors or director + CS).
revisionPoints: No common seal — two directors or director + CS

enhancement.definition: Section 22 deems bills, hundis and promissory notes made under company authority to be company instruments, and provides for written attorney authorisation (with or without common seal) so that deeds signed by the attorney bind the company.
